subject: Re: 🔵{Brand} & MobUpps
body:
Hi RECIPIENT_NAME,
Following up on my earlier note about scaling US payer cohorts for your mid-core and RPG titles. The one point worth repeating: we optimize against the first payer conversion through value-based bidding tied to revenue-tiered events, then hold the cohort through the early curve so spend compounds into D7 and D30. In US mid-core that has us near a D7 ROAS in the 4% to 5% band, the bar we calibrate against Supercell and Scopely. I can share the genre cohort view tuned to your title. Worth a short look?
angle: warm bump, restate payer-conversion proof (value-based bidding + cohort hold)
illustrative_flags: D7 ROAS in the 4% to 5% band (MobUpps, illustrative; calibrated to the NA mid-core market band ~4.5%)
register_notes: Stage 1 EN gaming_midcore_hardcore: references prior outreach in first sentence; restates single proof (payer-conversion optimization via value-based bidding + early-curve cohort hold); one illustrative MobUpps figure (D7 ROAS 4-5% band, held as a band, not audited); peers Supercell/Scopely reused from parent, no new brands; soft CTA, 1 question mark; no sign-off; native US register; no em dash; no X-not-Y.
